adjudication.rationale: In the added test `ECDSAAlgorithmTest`, a single EC keypair is generated once via `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair()` and then reused for ES256/ES384/ES512. The test only checks that `asn1derToConcatenatedRS` and `concatenatedRSToASN1DER` round-trip (`Assert.assertArrayEquals(rsConcat, rsConcat2)`) and never performs `Signature.verify` on the DER re-encoded signature, so it can stay green even if the conversion is incompatible with real signatures for the expected curve/length (especially since `signLength` is taken from the algorithm enum, not from the actual key/curve used). This is a specific, diff-grounded test coverage gap rather than a runtime defect.

adjudication.rationale: In AuthzClientCryptoProvider#getEcdsaCryptoProvider().concatenatedRSToASN1DER(byte[] signature, int signLength), the code blindly does System.arraycopy(signature, 0, r, 1, len) and System.arraycopy(signature, len, s, 1, len) where len = signLength/2. There is no check that signature.length == signLength. If signature is shorter than signLength, arraycopy will throw an unchecked ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException; if signature is longer, the extra trailing bytes are ignored because only the first signLength bytes are copied.

adjudication_records.issue_text: common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java:57 — Multiple-provider hard failure replaced by silent selection, and Default/FIPS/Elytron all return order 200, so a default+FIPS classpath now picks one nondeterministically (ServiceLoader order) with only a debug log instead of failing.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes CryptoIntegration.detectProvider to no longer throw when multiple CryptoProvider implementations are found; it now sorts by CryptoProvider::order (descending) and returns the first, only emitting debug logs for the rest. However, DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider all implement order() to return 200 in this diff, so when more than one of these is on the classpath the selection is effectively determined by ServiceLoader discovery/encounter order (tie on sort key), rather than being unambiguous. This can silently pick the wrong provider (e.g., non-FIPS vs FIPS) compared to the previous hard-failure behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/AuthzClient.java:95 — AuthzClient.create now globally and irrevocably initializes the JVM-wide CryptoIntegration singleton using AuthzClient's classloader, a new side effect that can pin the stub AuthzClientCryptoProvider (most methods throw UnsupportedOperationException) for other Keycloak libraries in the same classloader.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a new global side effect: AuthzClient.create(Configuration) now calls CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader()) before constructing the client. CryptoIntegration uses a JVM-wide static provider selection (singleton-style) and detects providers via ServiceLoader with the given classloader; with the new authz-client META-INF/services entry, AuthzClientCryptoProvider becomes eligible. AuthzClientCryptoProvider implements only a small subset (many methods throw UnsupportedOperationException), so if it ends up being the selected provider in an application that also uses other Keycloak code relying on unimplemented CryptoProvider methods, that could cause runtime failures. However, the diff also introduces provider ordering and sets Default/FIPS/Elytron providers to order()=200 vs AuthzClientCryptoProvider order()=100, so in a classpath that includes the full crypto modules the stub provider should be deprioritized, making this more of an architectural/side-effect concern than a clearly verifiable defect from the diff alone.

In `AuthzClientCryptoProvider`, many required `CryptoProvider` methods do indeed throw `UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported yet.")` (e.g., `getAlgorithmProvider`, `getCertificateUtils`, `getPemUtils`, `getSignature`, etc.), which means any runtime path that invokes those methods would fail with a generic message. However, the diff does not show any concrete call sites that will hit those stubs, so it’s not a provable broken behavior from the diff alone—more an architectural/completeness concern introduced by registering an intentionally limited provider without explicit signaling in the exception messages.

adjudication_records.issue_text: common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java:57 — Provider precedence is set by magic order values (100 here, 200 hardcoded in each of three providers) with no named constants, and when two providers share 200 the winner is silently decided by ServiceLoader order (the old error on duplicates was removed).

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes CryptoIntegration.detectProvider to sort providers by CryptoProvider::order (descending) and no longer throws when multiple providers are present; it just picks foundProviders.get(0) and logs others (common/.../CryptoIntegration.java). At the same time, three different built-in providers all return the same order value 200 (DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, FIPS1402Provider), so when more than one is on the classpath the chosen provider is determined by whatever ServiceLoader iteration order yields after a stable sort, i.e., an effectively arbitrary/tie-broken-by-load-order selection. This is a behavior change from the previous explicit error and can lead to incorrect provider selection in multi-provider classpaths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java:69 — The ignored-providers message is built with a manual StringBuilder that leaves a trailing ", ", and it is passed to debugf as a format string.

adjudication.rationale: In CryptoIntegration.detectProvider, the code does build a StringBuilder with a trailing ", " and passes builder.toString() to logger.debugf(...). However, this is a minor log-format/style nit rather than a verifiable functional defect introduced by the diff: the trailing comma only affects debug output, and the format-string risk is speculative (provider class names are not shown to contain format specifiers in the diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/ASN1Decoder.java:131 — readLength() returns -1 for indefinite-length encoding, but readSequence/readNext never handle -1, so this branch is effectively dead or misleading.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added ASN1Decoder.readLength(), the method explicitly returns -1 for indefinite-length encoding (length == 0x80). However, callers don’t handle this sentinel: readSequence() sets `int length = readLength();` and then loops `while (length > 0)`, so a -1 length yields an empty sequence without consuming any content; readNext() does `int length = readLength(); length += reset();`, so a -1 length produces an incorrect read size (`reset()-1`). This makes the indefinite-length branch incorrect/misleading and can cause wrong parsing if such input is encountered.

adjudication_records.issue_text: common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java:57 — Removing the multiple-provider fail-fast means providers with equal order (Default/FIPS/Elytron all 200) are now picked nondeterministically by ServiceLoader order, logged only at debug, so a FIPS deployment can silently run on the non-FIPS provider.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider` to no longer throw when multiple `CryptoProvider`s are found; it now sorts by `CryptoProvider::order` descending and returns the first provider, logging the rest only at debug. However, the diff also sets `order()` to `200` for `DefaultCryptoProvider`, `FIPS1402Provider`, and `WildFlyElytronProvider`, so when more than one of these is on the classpath, the comparator treats them as equal and the selected provider depends on the underlying `ServiceLoader` iteration order (not guaranteed). This can silently select a non-FIPS provider even if a FIPS provider is present, whereas previously it would fail fast.

adjudication_records.issue_text: common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoProvider.java:44 — New abstract order() without a default makes any existing third-party CryptoProvider compiled against the old interface throw AbstractMethodError inside detectProvider's sort, failing CryptoIntegration.init entirely.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `int order();` to `org.keycloak.common.crypto.CryptoProvider` with no default implementation, and `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider(...)` now unconditionally sorts providers via `Comparator.comparingInt(CryptoProvider::order).reversed()`. Any third-party `CryptoProvider` implementation compiled against the previous interface (without `order()`) would load via `ServiceLoader` but throw `AbstractMethodError` when the sort invokes `order()`, preventing `CryptoIntegration.init(...)` from completing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:109 — concatenatedRSToASN1DER does not validate signature.length against signLength, so malformed input throws unchecked ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of the declared IOException.

adjudication.rationale: In AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getEcdsaCryptoProvider().concatenatedRSToASN1DER, the method copies `len` bytes from `signature` into `r` and `s` via `System.arraycopy(signature, 0, r, 1, len)` and `System.arraycopy(signature, len, s, 1, len)` without checking `signature.length >= signLength` (or at least `>= 2*len`). If a caller passes a shorter/malformed `signature`, `System.arraycopy` will throw an unchecked IndexOutOfBounds/ArrayIndexOutOfBounds exception instead of the declared `IOException` path, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java:57 — Removing the multiple-provider error while Default, FIPS1402 and Elytron all share order 200 means that when both are on the classpath, whichever ServiceLoader lists first wins with only a debug log, so a FIPS deployment can silently end up running the non-FIPS DefaultCryptoProvider

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes CryptoIntegration.detectProvider to no longer throw when multiple CryptoProvider implementations are discovered. It now sorts providers by CryptoProvider::order descending and returns the first, only logging ignored providers at debug level. In this diff, DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider all implement order() returning 200, so the sort does not break ties; the selected provider will depend on ServiceLoader discovery/encounter order. This can cause a FIPS environment with multiple providers on the classpath to silently select a non-FIPS provider (e.g., DefaultCryptoProvider) instead of failing fast, which is a correctness/security issue introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:103 — concatenatedRSToASN1DER never checks signature.length == signLength, so untrusted JWS signatures with extra trailing bytes still verify (malleable) and short ones throw an unchecked ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException

adjudication.rationale: In AuthzClientCryptoProvider#getEcdsaCryptoProvider().concatenatedRSToASN1DER, it blindly copies `len` bytes twice from `signature` via `System.arraycopy(signature, 0, r, 1, len)` and `System.arraycopy(signature, len, s, 1, len)` without validating `signature.length == signLength`. If `signature.length > signLength`, trailing bytes are ignored and the DER encoding is produced from only the first `signLength` bytes; if `signature.length < signLength`, `System.arraycopy` can throw an unchecked `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`. Both behaviors are directly verifiable from the diff and can lead to accepting non-canonical signatures / crashing on malformed input.

adjudication_records.issue_text: authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/ASN1Decoder.java:133 — Lenient DER parser: it accepts indefinite length (-1, which makes readInteger throw NegativeArraySizeException), ignores the tag class and constructed bit, and ignores trailing data after the SEQUENCE and INTEGER elements

adjudication.rationale: In newly added ASN1Decoder.readLength(), the method explicitly returns -1 for indefinite-length encoding (when first length byte is 0x80). Callers like readInteger() then do `byte[] bytes = read(length);` which will allocate `new byte[length]` in read(int), causing a NegativeArraySizeException for length == -1. Also, tag validation in readSequence()/readInteger() only checks `tagNo` derived from `tag & 0x1f` and does not validate the universal class / constructed bit (e.g., a non-universal tag with low bits 0x10 or 0x02 would be accepted). Finally, readSequence() and readInteger() do not ensure all input is consumed (no check for remaining bytes after parsing), so trailing data is ignored. These behaviors are directly present in the diff and can lead to incorrect parsing / DoS on malformed input.

adjudication_records.issue_text: authz/client/src/test/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/test/ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java:72 — A single default "EC" key pair (P-256) is reused for ES384/ES512, so the real P-384/P-521 signature sizes (including the >127-byte long-form DER length for ES512) are never tested.

adjudication.rationale: In ECDSAAlgorithmTest, a single key pair is generated once via KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair() and reused for ES256/ES384/ES512. The diff does not specify curve parameters per algorithm (e.g., secp384r1 for ES384, secp521r1 for ES512), so the test does not ensure it exercises signatures from the expected key sizes/curves. As a result, edge cases tied to larger curves (including potentially larger DER encodings) may not be covered. This is a test coverage/accuracy concern rather than a production defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: authz/client/src/test/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/test/ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java:686 — The test only checks a DER->RS->DER->RS round trip; the DER that concatenatedRSToASN1DER produces is never compared to the JDK original or checked with Signature.verify, so symmetric encoder/decoder bugs would go unnoticed.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added ECDSAAlgorithmTest, the test signs data with the JDK (Signature.sign()), then only asserts a round-trip through the project’s own conversions: der -> asn1derToConcatenatedRS -> concatenatedRSToASN1DER -> asn1derToConcatenatedRS, and compares rsConcat to rsConcat2. It never checks that the DER produced by concatenatedRSToASN1DER matches the original JDK DER (sign) or that it can be verified via Signature.verify, so a symmetric bug in ASN1Encoder/ASN1Decoder or the conversion logic could pass unnoticed. This is a test coverage/completeness issue rather than a demonstrated defect. (The cited line number is inconsistent with the diff, but the substantive critique matches the shown test code.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: authz/client/src/test/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/test/ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java:676 — No deterministic edge-case vectors: r/s with the high bit set (needs a 0x00 pad), r/s with leading zero bytes (shorter than the curve size), and fixed known-answer signatures all rely on random keys.

adjudication.rationale: The newly added test `ECDSAAlgorithmTest` only performs a round-trip conversion (DER -> concatenated RS -> DER -> concatenated RS) using a randomly generated EC keypair and a signature produced at runtime (`KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair()` and `signature.sign()`). It does not include deterministic, fixed vectors that exercise edge conditions like r/s requiring 0x00 padding due to high-bit set, or r/s shorter than the curve size with leading zeros. This is a concrete test-gap for the newly added ASN.1 encode/decode logic in `AuthzClientCryptoProvider`/`ASN1Encoder`/`ASN1Decoder`, but it is not a verifiable functional defect by itself. (Also, the referenced line number `:676` does not match this new 74-line file.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:503 — Malformed-input paths have no tests: wrong sequence size, a non-INTEGER tag, truncated or out-of-bounds lengths, and indefinite length (-1) in the ASN1Decoder.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new ASN.1 parsing/encoding logic (ASN1Decoder/ASN1Encoder) used by AuthzClientCryptoProvider’s ECDSA conversion methods, and only adds a happy-path test (ECDSAAlgorithmTest) that round-trips valid signatures. There are no tests covering the decoder/consumer error paths that exist in the new code: e.g., ASN1Decoder.readSequence/readInteger tag validation, readLength truncated/out-of-bounds handling, and the consumer-side seq.size()!=2 check in asn1derToConcatenatedRS. The finding’s cited line number (503) doesn’t match the new file length, but the substance (missing malformed-input tests for these new branches) is diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java:57 — The behavior change from failing on multiple providers to picking by order() has no test showing that the higher-order provider (Default/Elytron/FIPS at 200) beats AuthzClientCryptoProvider (100) when both are on the classpath.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes CryptoIntegration.detectProvider to sort loaded CryptoProvider implementations by the new CryptoProvider.order() (reversed) and no longer throws when multiple providers are present, instead selecting foundProviders.get(0) and logging the rest. The PR also assigns order()=200 to Default/WildFlyElytron/FIPS providers and order()=100 to the new AuthzClientCryptoProvider. However, the only added test (ECDSAAlgorithmTest) exercises ECDSA signature conversions directly and does not cover CryptoIntegration provider selection when multiple providers are on the classpath, so the concern about missing test coverage for this new selection behavior is valid and diff-grounded.
